clue.text: Wrench outside container for plumbing ware

indicators.note: outside tells us the first piece sits around the second

parts.note: to wrench is to tug or pull hard
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Someone uses a wrench on the outside of a vessel used for plumbing supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrench' looks like a plumber's tool, but here it is a verb meaning pull hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipework of flexible or rigid tubes is the stock-in-trade of a plumber.

clue.text: Very emotive bird-song captivating hearts

indicators.note: captivating means holding prisoner, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: trilling is the warbling sound songbirds make
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A birdsong so moving that it wins over listeners' hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' puts H inside TRILLING, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exciting and stirring causes a surge of feeling, so it is strongly emotive.

clue.text: American retriever picked up good leftover bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters are lifted and so read from bottom to top

parts.note: an odd item is one left over, unmatched
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A dog fetches a leftover bone in the American manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns G + ODD + RIB to read upwards, giving the answer from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the US name for a gun dog trained to find and fetch game birds.

clue.text: No pieces to correct (outside Latin terms)

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so men means pieces

indicators.note: outside says the healing word goes around the abbreviation for the language

parts.note: to cure is to put right or correct

explanation.surface: A teacher declines to mark exercises, except for the Latin vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' are chessmen; the brackets make 'outside Latin terms' look like an aside, though 'terms' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of names or technical vocabulary in a field is a set of terms.

clue.text: Chant from faculty reverberating, led by bishop, maybe

indicators.note: led by means the following piece is preceded by the chess piece

parts.note: a bishop is one example of a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: reverberating suggests sound bouncing back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a faculty is a skill or knack, as is an art

explanation.surface: A chant echoes through the university faculty, headed by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests a university department but means a skill; 'bishop, maybe' points to a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeated sacred word or phrase in meditation or worship is a kind of chant.

clue.text: Sailor, one among others side by side

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: among places the single letter within the remainder

parts.note: the rest means the others
a means one

explanation.surface: A sailor stands with one group among others, all lined up together.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, an able seaman, is the standard crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level and alongside each other in a row is the plain sense here.

clue.text: Capital East European wine without a hint of Orvieto

indicators.note: without tells us to drop a letter from the wine's name

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

indicators.note: a hint gives just the opening letter of the Italian wine name

explanation.surface: A capital city's selection of Hungarian wine, lacking any trace of Italian Orvieto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the A from TOKAY to leave TOKY; 'a hint of' gives O, the first letter of Orvieto. Orvieto is an Italian white wine, a neat decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the seat of government of Japan, a capital city.

clue.text: Dressed for a storm making itself heard

indicators.note: making itself heard means the phrase is to be spoken out, its sound counted

parts.note: a storm is an attack, a raid

explanation.surface: A storm is brewing, its noise growing ever louder.
explanation.walkthrough: A storm in the military sense is an attack, a raid; 'a raid' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clothed or decked out in finery is to be attired, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Trade was modified with onset of preference

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the three letters are rearranged
onset is the start, so just the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Commerce changed once buyers began to show their preferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' turns WAS into SWA; 'onset of' gives P from preference.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange of one thing for another is a barter, a trade.

clue.text: They're beaten before the battle starts!

definitions.text: They're beaten before the battle starts!

parts.words: They're beaten before the battle starts!
parts.note: reads as troops defeated before fighting, but means percussion instruments struck as a call to fight

explanation.surface: An army loses before the fighting even begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' suggests defeat, but it is the drummer's beating, rousing soldiers before a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussion played to summon or rouse fighters before a conflict.

clue.text: Agent severed links with Russia

parts.note: to sever links with someone is to break off, so broke
R is the international vehicle code for Russia

explanation.surface: A spy cut his ties with Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a defecting spy, but agent here means a dealer acting for clients.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman who buys and sells on behalf of others acts as their agent.

clue.text: A way to make proper provisions

parts.note: proper in the sense of complete or utter, as in a proper mess, is thorough
fare is food and provisions

explanation.surface: Advice on how to supply decent rations.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public route through a place is a way.

clue.text: Sought sympathy, pained? He only got ridiculed

indicators.note: ridiculed means mocked, made a nonsense of, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone in pain who hoped for compassion received only mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculed' rearranges PAINED HE ONLY GOT into the fifteen letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerating one's suffering for effect is a bid for others' pity.

clue.text: Eccentric notable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strange or peculiar and exceptional or remarkable.

clue.text: Fabric with precious diamonds

parts.note: precious in the sense of affected or overly quaint is twee
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Cloth decorated with valuable gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precious' seems to describe jewels, but means affectedly dainty, as does 'twee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen cloth from Scotland, a classic fabric.

clue.text: Cite extra newly-issued release

indicators.note: newly-issued suggests the letters reissued in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A request to quote from an extra edition that has just come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-issued' rearranges CITE EXTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To free or disentangle someone from a difficulty is to release them.

clue.text: Record, I see, makes sound sense

parts.note: a log is a written record
the letter C is spoken like the word see

explanation.surface: Keeping a diary and noticing things is a sensible practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters I and C pronounced together say 'I see', the clue's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning that holds together is rational thought.

clue.text: Glowing, keen about bachelor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mourning word goes round the single letter

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to lament

explanation.surface: Someone is radiant and eager regarding an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LAMENT around B. 'keen' looks like eager, but means wail.
explanation.definitionFit: Softly radiant or flickering, as a flame playing over a surface.

clue.text: Fancy getting caught, on a charge

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a price is a charge

explanation.surface: Someone arrested and charged with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an arrest on a criminal charge, but charge is a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden whim is a passing fancy.

clue.text: Brass pieces from Thailand, strange idols

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
rum is an old British word for odd or strange
pets in the sense of favourites, people idolised

explanation.surface: Ornaments brought back from Thailand turn out to be odd brass idols.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM in British slang means peculiar; PETS are favourites, like teacher's pets.
explanation.definitionFit: These are wind instruments of the brass family.

clue.text: See state worker flag

parts.note: Penn is a short form of Pennsylvania, a US state
a worker ant, so ant means worker

explanation.surface: Look at the banner of the state's labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just introduces the wordplay; it is an instruction to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tapering banner on a ship or at a sports ground is a kind of flag.

clue.text: Wrongful arrest based on false impression?

definitions.meaning: a mistaken apprehension, taking someone into custody in error

explanation.definitionFit: Read in two parts it is a mistaken seizure by police; read whole it is a misunderstanding.

clue.text: Hawk circling western rise

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the trading word encloses the letter

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A bird of prey circles above as the west wind rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts SELL around W. 'Hawk' looks like the bird, but here means peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge or increase, as of the sea or of feeling, is a rise.

clue.text: Comfortable place in Vine Street

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the street name

explanation.surface: A cosy home to be found on Vine Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning vi-NE ST-reet.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug home or refuge, like a bird's, is a cosy spot.

clue.text: Paradisal retreat engulfed by melting ice

indicators.note: engulfed by means swallowed up within the surrounding letters
melting suggests the frozen word losing its shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A hideaway swallowed by melting ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting' gives the anagram EIC of the frozen word, which then swallows the hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the Garden of Eden, so blissful and heavenly.

clue.text: A river in Irish county's where you'll find holiday homes

indicators.note: in puts the article and river letter inside the county's name

parts.note: Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: A river in Ireland where holidaymakers come to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places A and R inside CAVAN'S after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile homes towed or parked at a site are used for vacations.

clue.text: Ploughman keeping lines in line

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the row word contains the doubled letter

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps the furrows straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughman' suggests a person, but the steering lever on a boat shares the spelling; here it is one who tills.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tills the soil works the land with a plough.

clue.text: The twig's first to burn

indicators.note: first places the understanding word in front of the article

parts.note: to twig is to understand, to see

explanation.surface: The thin branch is the first to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twig' is British slang for realise, not a small branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with anger, to burn inside.
